findings.title: User action needed · Retrieve a known preference
findings.observed: During the 0.2.102 voice test, Samantha queried the Ledger and then said she had no saved site profile, although an active site-scoped preference already existed.
findings.recommendation: When a preference is relevant to a choice, recall its active scope and rule automatically and apply it without asking the user to name Context Ledger.
findings.verification: Spoken retest: Ledger returned the saved preference without being named; Samantha acted and the user independently confirmed seeing the expected Netflix profile.

details.Controlled follow-up: The 0.2.102 helper was exercised against the actual Ledger with a bounded selection stub: the same lookup without site scope returned zero records, while a site-scoped lookup returned two. The scoped path can read the existing records; the actual live request scope is unknown.
details.Lookup audit: The Ledger access audit recorded a concrete query naming the site and profile choice and returned zero results at the exact time of the voice lookup. It does not retain the request scope, so the reason that specific lookup missed the record is still unproven.
details.Latest test: The session record shows an initial profile question, then an explicit request to use saved preferences, followed by a zero-match recall. The owner named the choice; Samantha reported selecting it. No independent page readback was captured.
details.Scope discrepancy: A newly saved preference from that session was independently read back under the browser tool scope; earlier matching decisions were saved under the site tool scope. The failed recall scope and rule were not retained, so the precise reason for the miss is not proven. Personal values and identifiers are omitted.
details.Root cause analysis: The voice-facing Live instructions allow brief clarifications to be answered directly; the proactive Ledger instruction lives in the backend instructions and does not guarantee backend delegation at a preference-sensitive choice. Exact-scope and exact-rule recall is brittle: controlled reads found saved decisions with their precise scope and rule, but equivalent site identifiers or a different rule returned none. The actual live recall scope and rule were not recorded, so its specific mismatch is unknown.
details.Required fix: Ensure preference-sensitive choices reach the backend before asking; resolve site identity independently of browser tool, search existing scoped decisions without guessing a rule, and apply only an unambiguous active match. Record bounded scope/rule and delegation metadata to diagnose misses, without recording private values. Verify save, recall and application on an installed build.
details.Fix plan: The existing PR #87 implementation plan now includes a scoped automatic-preference milestone, known limits, failure handling, privacy boundaries, owner paths and installed acceptance checks. Legacy browser-scope migration and the voice decision-boundary signal remain open design decisions.
details.0.2.103 candidate: Adds explicit voice delegation guidance and a bounded same-scope candidate search when an exact rule misses. Candidates require disambiguation and do not establish a saved preference by themselves. Site alias resolution, deterministic voice routing, conflict handling and live acceptance remain open.

findings.observed: A real Codex CLI Luna run produced task usage, but T3-delegated child usage has not been linked to an authoritative session or an independent task acceptance result.
findings.recommendation: Establish a verifiable exact run, provider thread and turn-boundary binding; collect complete usage with explicit retry and child coverage; bind a separately verified result; reject incompatible or incomplete comparisons. Prove direct Codex first; keep T3 attribution unknown when no supported binding exists.

details.Scope and next action: Use provider-native usage events when controlling an explicit Codex thread. T3-provider-neutral attribution requires a supported T3 execution-to-provider usage interface; do not infer identities by time or mark complete without independent acceptance.
details.Native provider proof: Codex CLI 0.167.0 app-server resumed a known completed Codex test thread and emitted thread/tokenUsage/updated for the exact thread. Its cumulative input, cached-input, output and reasoning counters matched the previously observed terminal usage. Plain thread/read produced no usage notification in the bounded test; account/usage/read returned null threadUsage for this account. Resume is stateful and this proof covers one Codex thread only.
details.Control-plane limitation: T3 native provider analytics distinguish T3-managed child runs and native subagents but are documented as best effort, including possible missing children and restart gaps. The installed T3 CLI thread show and exposed MCP read did not return provider session ID or usage for the test child. No public provider-neutral exact-run usage API has been proved in this session.
details.Remaining work: Test marker propagation for an actual T3 task and verify uniqueness, lifecycle and spoofing limits. Establish authoritative task-to-artifact binding, verifier independence, child coverage and comparable cohort evidence before any savings verdict.
details.Evidence privacy and replay: Version 0.1.26 added optional quiet capture, rejected unexpected stored fields, and suppresses totals for ambiguous replayed or failed turns. Raw events are still forwarded unless --quiet-events is requested; comprehensive schema, all retry cases and privacy of existing records remain unverified.
details.Independent acceptance: A caller-supplied --verify exit code is a check result, not independent acceptance. Bind a separately executed verifier, scenario, output digest and verifier identity; absent or mismatched evidence must yield incomplete.
details.Next controlled checks: Run a disposable direct Codex task with a separately executed verifier and verify the exact native usage and output independently. Then attempt T3 via supported interfaces; report binding_unavailable when no authoritative run-to-thread-and-turn binding exists.
details.Next work: Developer Observability: full T3/child/retry attribution remains unresolved. findings.title: Gateway health times out after the voice process has already stopped
findings.observed: On 14 Nov 2026 at 01:16:24 IST, session bd4abacd logged startup/gateway_health failure 'timeout 45s' (observability col-97ca2e1ef5264965, ACU 0.2.141). The supervisor had already stopped the voice process at 01:15:39 IST, about 45 seconds earlier. Port 8766 is not listening after that failed start; CUAService is still running.
findings.recommendation: Cancel the gateway health wait when the voice process exits, and do not record a 45s timeout as a startup failure after an intentional or racing stop.

details.Expected: A start that is stopped within a second should not wait 45s and then log gateway_health failure.
details.Session: bd4abacd (supervisor only; no user or assistant turns)
details.Current state: Nothing is listening on 127.0.0.1:8766; Samantha appears off. CUAService is still running.
details.Root cause: start() was still in waitForGatewayHealth(timeout: 45) when stop() set stopping=true and process=nil at 01:15:39 IST. The wait loop only returns early on `if let proc = process, !proc.isRunning`, so a nil process is skipped and it keeps polling /health until the 45s deadline, after which start() logs timeout 45s.
details.Where to look: plugins/agent-computer-use/skills/macos-cua/service/Sources/CUAService/VoiceSupervisor.swift — start(), stop(), and waitForGatewayHealth(timeout:). stop() sets stopping, but the wait loop does not check it.

findings.title: The workflow strip and Last reported time don't move while new work is happening
findings.summary: The page stayed on Report & roll over with a Last reported time more than 30 minutes old while a fix was already running.
findings.impact: It looks as if work has finished or hasn't started, so you can't tell that a fix cycle is underway.
findings.done_when: Whenever the tracker is updated, the workflow strip and Last reported time show that latest activity, including during Plan & fix, Install, Verify and Report.
findings.observed: On 14 Nov 2026, the PR #107 page stayed on Report & roll over with Last reported 12:53 PM IST and a raw ISO timestamp next to Now, more than 30 minutes after live-details work had started. The strip only moved after the tracker was updated by hand.
findings.recommendation: At render time, Last reported and Now must reflect the newest tracker activity plus the render time, in IST, with no raw ISO as visible text. Every tracker write should advance the workflow timestamp, and the viewer should show the new stage as soon as the JSON changes.

findings.title: A fix cycle can start without a tracked finding in progress
findings.summary: Work on a fix can begin before that issue is logged on the change list, so the page doesn't show what's being fixed.
findings.impact: The agent can drift off the list, and you have no orderly record of what is in progress.
findings.done_when: A fix cycle cannot quietly start with no in-progress finding: the plugin refuses or flags it, and the skill tells the agent to log the finding first.
findings.observed: On 14 Nov 2026, 0.1.13 implementation work started in a new branch before a finding for that work was on the PR #107 change list. Guru asked that every issue being fixed be tracked and shown as in progress under Plan & fix.
findings.recommendation: Add a manage_findings guard that refuses or flags a fix-cycle stage (plan_fix, install, verify) when no finding is in progress, and state in SKILL.md that a fix cycle starts only after the finding is logged and set in progress.
